market_name: Will 9 Fed rate cuts happen in 2026?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether the probability shift is corroborated by front-end rate futures (SOFR/Fed funds futures) or is isolated Polymarket noise.
time_plan.1h: Compare 2y/10y Treasury yield moves and TLT price action to confirm a genuine dovish repricing versus thin-market drift.
time_plan.2h: Look for any macro headline (labor, credit, geopolitical) explaining a recession/easing narrative; if none, downgrade conviction.
time_plan.6h: Reassess vs equity risk sentiment and VIX — real 9-cut pricing should coincide with risk-off.
time_plan.12h: Evaluate whether yields sustained the move into the US session close; flag as noise if reversed.

predictions.reasoning: A market pricing 9 Fed cuts (225bps) in 2026 is an extreme easing/recession tail. If its implied probability spiked, it would signal expectations of aggressive Fed easing, typically triggered by a severe growth shock or crisis. That pushes front-end and long-end yields lower, lifting long-duration Treasury prices (TLT). The mapping is directionally clean but the signal is a low-probability tail, so any move is likely small over 12h and dwarfed by scheduled data/Fed communication.

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check DXY and rate-differential moves against the prediction-market shift.
time_plan.1h: Determine whether risk-off haven flows (dollar up) are competing with rate-differential effects (dollar down).
time_plan.2h: Cross-check EUR and JPY behavior to isolate the dominant driver.
time_plan.6h: Reassess with any crisis headlines that could flip the dollar to safe-haven bid.

predictions.reasoning: Aggressive Fed easing expectations (9 cuts) narrow US rate differentials versus other central banks, typically weakening the dollar. However, a 9-cut scenario often accompanies a global crisis, in which the dollar can strengthen on safe-haven demand — so the direction is ambiguous and confidence is low.

evidence_used: Market question implies 9 cuts (225bps) of Fed easing in 2026, an extreme dovish/recession tail
Standard macro linkage: aggressive Fed easing lowers Treasury yields and narrows rate differentials
Emergency-cut clause implies crisis scenarios are in scope
uncertainty_notes: 9 cuts is a low-probability tail; sharp moves in such markets are often thin-liquidity noise
A 9-cut scenario may reflect crisis, which flips the dollar to safe-haven strength — opposite of the rate-differential effect
The 700bps tradable threshold vastly exceeds realistic 12h moves in these liquid proxies, so neither prediction is tradable

llm_justification.summary: A rising implied probability that the Fed delivers 9 cuts in 2026 signals expectations of aggressive easing, usually tied to a severe growth or crisis shock. The cleanest downstream implication is lower Treasury yields (TLT up); a weaker dollar is plausible but ambiguous because crisis-driven easing can produce safe-haven dollar strength. Both moves are directionally supported but small over 12h, well below the 700bps tradable bar, and the underlying signal is a low-probability tail prone to noise.
key_assumptions: A probability shift in this market reflects genuine easing expectations rather than Polymarket-specific liquidity noise
Standard rate-transmission channels hold: more expected cuts => lower yields
The move is not already fully priced into rate futures
failure_modes: The prediction-market move is thin-market noise with no real macro information
9-cut pricing accompanies a crisis, flipping the dollar to safe-haven strength (thesis inverts for UUP)
Information is already public via Fed funds futures, so no incremental asset move
TLT/UUP are broad proxies whose 12h moves are dominated by unrelated data releases
Expected magnitudes are far below the 700bps tradable threshold — not actionable
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
